invariant: Private thread writes require the owning principal (agent JWT sub == thread.agent_id) regardless of transport
counterexample: Register agent A and agent B; A stakes via REST creating thr-X; call MCP market.message with B's api_key on thr-X
evidence: app/mcp_bridge.py:670-689 — _agent_from_key authenticates B, but no check that thread.agent_id == agent.agent_id; insert_thread_message runs unconditionally; tests/test_h5_falsifier.py::test_mcp_market_message_foreign_thread_write FAILS with status 'sent'
required_correction: Add thread.get('agent_id') != agent['agent_id'] -> error; also enforce thread.status == 'open' parity with REST (kassa.py:641-642)

invariant: Closed threads refuse new messages on every write path
counterexample: Stake -> thread; set status='closed' via store; call MCP market.message with the owning agent's api_key
evidence: app/mcp_bridge.py:670-689 has no status check; REST post_thread_message rejects at kassa.py:641-642; test FAILS: message inserted into closed thread
required_correction: Add `if thread.get('status') != 'open': return {'error': 'Thread is closed'}` before insert

invariant: Poster credential (?magic= token) must be deliverable on every thread-creation path
counterexample: Call MCP market.stake; inspect result, emitted events, and code path for token delivery
evidence: app/mcp_bridge.py:606-653 generates magic_token, stores _hash_key(magic_token), then drops the plaintext — no send_magic_link call, no return field, no operator alert. REST path emails it (kassa.py:380-390). Poster can never authenticate to an MCP-created thread; thread is a write-only dead end
reproduction: tests/test_h5_falsifier.py::test_mcp_stake_thread_poster_can_never_auth (documents: hash stored, ?magic=any-guess -> 403, no delivery mechanism in code)
required_correction: Send send_magic_link to thread.poster_email (async, fire-and-forget like REST) or fall back to notify_agent when poster is a registered agent
retest: After fix, poster magic link delivered; add a mock-send assertion

invariant: Thread-body visibility is confined to authenticated thread participants (thread_hub) and notified counterparties
counterexample: Agent sends market.message via MCP; observe emits and notifications
evidence: app/mcp_bridge.py:676-689 inserts the message but emits no state.emit('kassa_thread_message'), no thread_hub.broadcast, no send_message_notification, no notify_agent — REST path does all four (kassa.py:689-782). Poster watching /ws/thread/{id} never sees the agent's MCP reply in real time and is never emailed
reproduction: Code inspection diff of kassa.py:635-784 vs mcp_bridge.py:656-689
required_correction: Mirror REST post-commit side effects: thread_hub.broadcast, public-safe kassa_thread_message envelope, poster notification
retest: Test ws listener receives MCP-originated thread_message

invariant: PII submitted via public write paths must not be readable by unauthenticated clients
counterexample: POST /api/kassa/contact with from_email PII; POST /api/inbox/apply with applicant name; then GET /api/audit with no credentials
evidence: kassa.py:1296-1300 logs from_email into audit; operator.py:273 logs applicant name; operator.py:218 logs contact name+subject; core.py:127-129 serves GET /api/audit unauthenticated returning full entries; test asserts both PII values present in the public feed
required_correction: Either admin-gate GET /api/audit (add '/api/audit' to _ADMIN_GET_PREFIXES) or scrub PII fields in audit.log calls for public-write paths
retest: Repeat test; expect PII absent or 403

invariant: audit_event broadcasts must carry the row the endpoint logged, not an arbitrary newer row
counterexample: Endpoint logs audit row A; a concurrent public write logs PII row B; endpoint then emits audit.recent(1) which returns B onto hub+public_hub
evidence: All call sites use state.audit.recent(1)[0] at emit time (e.g. core.py:187, kassa.py:200); emit() broadcasts to unauthenticated public_hub (deps.py:53-58); race is real under concurrent load though not deterministic
required_correction: Capture the log entry's id/object at log time and emit that exact entry, or include entry id and filter
retest: Emit payload identity matches logged row under interleaved writes

invariant: Thread-returning endpoints strip poster credential material consistently
evidence: kassa.py:610 strips magic_token/magic_token_plain for single-thread GET; kassa.py:585-587 returns raw rows including 'magic_token' (sha256 hash) and 'poster_email' to the staking agent; verified live: dict_keys include magic_token
required_correction: Apply the same dict-comprehension strip used at line 610 to the list endpoint
retest: magic_token key absent from list rows

invariant: Agent self-service endpoints must be reachable by their documented principal
counterexample: Agent calls DELETE /api/kassa/stakes/{stake_id} with valid JWT expecting withdraw
evidence: server.py:348-363 — DELETE not under _PUBLIC_WRITE_PREFIXES and '/api/kassa/stakes' not under _OPERATOR_WRITE_PREFIXES, so agents get 403 at middleware before reaching the handler's ownership check (kassa.py:439-448). Pre-existing (not introduced by H5 GET-prefix change) but inside the same lane surface
reproduction: Trace middleware prefix sets; DELETE /api/kassa/stakes/stk-x with Bearer JWT -> 403 'admin_key_required'
required_correction: Add '/api/kassa/stakes' to a bearer-authorized write prefix (handler already verifies ownership via JWT sub)
retest: DELETE with agent JWT reaches handler (200/403 ownership), not middleware 403

evidence: mcp_bridge.py:595-653: no duplicate-stake 409 (REST kassa.py:299-302), no kassa_stake event, no operator alert, no notify_agent to poster-agent, amount accepted but never persisted
